## What this letter says
This letter is from one doctor to another doctor (Dr. CD). It is about you. You are a 19-year-old man. Dr. CD saw you in 2005 for a possible seizure (suspected seizure activity).

You have had no seizures for the past 2 1/2 years. You take Dilantin. You have asked to come off Dilantin.

The letter asks Dr. CD to look at you. Dr. CD is asked to say if you need to keep taking Dilantin. No decision has been made.

The letter says your nerve exam (neurological exam) is normal. Your Dilantin level is slightly low at 12.5. The letter gives no unit for this number.

In 2005, the note said the true cause of your episodes was not clear. Doctors thought about whether to reconsider the medicine.

You will probably need another EEG (a recording of the brain's electrical activity). This is only probable.

## What you need to do
1. The letter does not list any tasks for you.
2. Dr. CD is asked to give advice on Dilantin.
3. The letter asks that the repeat EEG be arranged through Health Center.
4. Any other tests should be arranged at Health Center before they are booked.

## Dates and medicines
- 2005: Dr. CD saw you for a possible seizure.
- The letter gives no date for the letter or for any visit.
- Dilantin, 300 milligrams, daily. You are continuing this dose.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- Do I need to keep taking Dilantin?
- Will I need another EEG?
- What does my Dilantin level of 12.5 mean?
- When will I hear what Dr. CD advises?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
